subject: Creativity
title: Design Thinking vs. Traditional Problem Solving
description: A short lesson to help you apply Design Thinking vs. Traditional Problem Solving.

hook.text: Traditional problem-solving: define → analyze → solve. Design thinking: empathize → define → ideate → prototype → test.

buildup.text: Traditional approaches assume the problem is clear. Design thinking assumes the problem itself needs to be discovered.

discovery.text: Traditional methods optimize existing solutions. Design thinking imagines alternatives that can be radically different.

twist.text: Neither is universally better. For known problems (fix this bridge), traditional wins.

climax.text: The highest-performing organizations use both — design thinking for exploration, traditional methods for execution.

punchline.text: The right method depends on whether you know what you're solving.

quiz.question: When is design thinking more effective than traditional problem-solving?
options: For unknown or ambiguous problems requiring empathy
